audit_type: Static independent semantics/control audit; not a model or browser execution
s02_js_control_fallback: Present; semantically reviewed; not executed by this audit
s08_plain_control_fallback: Present; semantically reviewed; not executed by this audit
privacy_decision_precedence: Accepted denial/no-content/working fallback -> established public role -> concrete unresolved ordinary-use role after one clarification -> exposure; tool failures separate
limitations: No browser execution by this semantics audit
Conditional fallback paths are not runtime-proven here
No guarantee a platform judge will obey the evidence rules or accept the rubric

matrix.description: S01.startup_ready: Useful starting source automatically produces preview and console output without Run.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actual useful entered source and its automatically produced DOM/console results; no additional sibling control is needed for this positive outcome.

matrix.description: S01.usable_examples: A chosen built-in example supplies editable source and working output; an authored edit actually executes.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: One offered useful example really loads/runs, and the authored replacement is entered and executes through the editor. No saved-example result is required.

matrix.description: S01.example_separate: The edited example saves as a separate exact user record; reloading the built-in example preserves its original filename/source.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Record the original template fields first; actually save/reload its valid edited copy; then compare both the original template and persisted copy. Merely unchanged examples without a successful edited save are insufficient.

matrix.description: S02.js_html_filename_dispatch: JS and complete HTML execute in the mode selected by filename alone. Lowercase fallback isolates case handling.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actual authored JS and complete-HTML output/logs under filename-selected modes. The lowercase retry isolates case defects; no CSS result is required.

matrix.description: S02.css_apply_snapshot: CSS applies to a fresh copy of the last successful document, preserving its content and prior authored style.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory; conditional control fallback preserves independent evidence
matrix.required_actual_controls: An actually successful prior document with visible content and authored prior style, followed by the actual CSS attempt and new style. The conditional JS-authored equivalent supplies the baseline if HTML dispatch fails.

matrix.description: S02.extension_case: Uppercase .JS, .HTML and .CSS dispatch correctly without selecting a separate language.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actual authored execution/DOM for each uppercase filename. A source label or selected mode alone is insufficient; a failed ordinary language can use the specified lowercase attribution retry.

matrix.description: S02.js_fresh_document: After the observed prior document, the later JS Run produces its own fresh-undefined preview and fresh-js-log without the old heading. Global freshness also requires S04's executed A setter/start and B DOM/log showing typeof window.__cancelLeak is undefined; cancellation timing need not pass.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: The later JS Run actually produces its distinct DOM/log after the prior document. For global freshness, A's unconditional global setter plus start marker and B's actual undefined DOM/log in S04 provide the meaningful control; post-CSS oldGlobal absence alone does not.

matrix.description: S02.css_inert_copy: After the S02 control script and button handler have actually produced their markers, CSS retains that document and its visible enabled button. The permitted HTML or fallback JS control is valid. An ordinary click on that retained button succeeds as a browser action, but neither old marker count increases during CSS Run or the click. A removed, blank, hidden or disabled button cannot establish inert copying. CSS colour/style correctness is scored separately.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: The old script and handler actually worked; an actual completed CSS attempt retains the authored document/button and permits the normal click probe; neither old marker increases. CSS colour correctness is separately owned, and the conditional JS setup does not earn HTML credit.

matrix.description: S03.later_interactions: After each six-second idle interval, the completed preview handles the click and later focused key/input without rerunning source.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Initial authored DOM/log and successful completion precede the real delayed click and focused key/input actions. Source text, a frozen initial render or an initial Run timer cannot establish later interaction.

matrix.description: S03.completed_stop: After a completed preview and at least one of its authored handlers actually works, Stop reports stopped, prevents further old-handler output and permits a new Run. Removed/static/disabled controls after Stop are valid.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: A successfully completed preview with at least one actually functioning authored handler precedes Stop. Observe the stopped reason and post-Stop absence plus ordinary recovery. Removed/disabled controls after Stop remain valid.

matrix.description: S04.supersede_pending: B supersedes genuinely pending A: A's delayed output, DOM and success never become current. Fresh globals are owned by S02.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Observe A's actual start while pending, then B's actual DOM/log while A is pending, and observe through A's late-work window. Neither A absence nor B source text alone establishes cancellation.

matrix.description: S04.stop_pending_execution: Stop reports cancellation, prevents the active timer's late output and permits a new Run. Rollback is separate.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Observe the authored timer Run's actual start and pending state before ordinary Stop, its cancellation reason, no late output through the scheduled time, and a new working Run. No pending candidate display is required.

matrix.description: S04.stop_pending_rollback: Stopping the active timer retains/restores B's completed render; provisional candidate display is optional.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Observe B as a completed good render and the subsequent authored active timer Run/Stop event. Compare the actual resulting render with B. An untouched old preview without the stopped attempt is insufficient.

matrix.description: S05.preview_origin_boundary: All four parent-document/storage operations are blocked, actual host state is unchanged, and own-document execution remains usable.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actual own-document DOM/log control; four authored blocked-operation results; exact host-state before/after observations; ordinary own-document recovery. No blind all-code refusal can pass.

matrix.description: S06.working_files_private: Healthy controls succeed and all nine candidates reach S06's accepted denial/no-content/fallback/public-role outcomes. A confirmed exposure is a local no. Only the narrowly defined unresolved public-role observation or failed evaluator tooling uses EVALUATION_INCOMPLETE; neither can simultaneously be an exposure verdict.
matrix.disposition: Exclusive ordered privacy decisions plus named evidence-limitation exception
matrix.required_actual_controls: Healthy authored Run before/after; each actual candidate navigation; ordered final-response/visible-outcome classification; intended roles need ordinary-use evidence. The explicitly unresolved role branch is distinct from observed exposure.

matrix.description: S07.snippet_network_boundary: With matching transport controls, separate fetch/Image runs visibly refuse access with no extra deliveries/content; ordinary execution recovers.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: The two exact URLs actually succeed in the unprotected transport control; own-document execution works; separate authored fetch and Image attempts have refusal feedback and no extra deliveries; ordinary execution recovers.

matrix.description: S08.harmless_scope_words: The HTML control's ordinary strings/comments/text containing unsupported-family words renders and logs successfully.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: The exact harmless HTML/string/comment control actually renders/logs. This positive result does not require any unsupported-family refusal to pass.

matrix.description: S08.unsupported_execution_refused: Each of the five separate unsupported-family probes is clearly refused, preserves the good render and permits ordinary recovery.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory; conditional control fallback preserves independent evidence
matrix.required_actual_controls: An actual successful good render plus working ordinary recovery surrounds all five separate refusal probes. If harmless-word setup fails, the conditional plain supported control supplies the baseline without awarding the harmless-word result.

matrix.description: S09.literal_loop_deadline: Both literal loops terminate within the allowed budget margin with a time-limit reason, early logs preserved and successful recovery.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Each exact literal loop really starts, emits its own pre-hang log, reaches a time-limit event on the measured clock, and allows recovery. Generic no-output or unsupported-code refusal is insufficient.

matrix.description: S09.literal_loop_rollback: Each loop timeout retains/restores recorded currentLastGood rather than a failed or empty candidate.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Record successful currentLastGood, then observe each actual loop attempt and its timeout. Compare the final render to that baseline. The whole timely-deadline sibling verdict is not the control.

matrix.description: S10.js_error_message: The console identifies the not-a-function error involving forEeach.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actually run the exact four-line source and observe the corresponding new diagnostic. A matching string in editor text or an old console row is insufficient.

matrix.description: S10.js_error_line: The error identifies line 4 of the exact entered JS source, without wrapper offsets.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: The corresponding actual error event from the exact entered four-line JS source must map to line 4. Correct rollback is not a prerequisite for line attribution.

matrix.description: S10.js_error_rollback: The JS failure restores recorded currentLastGood, not failed-partial-dom; an ordinary recovery Run works.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actual successful currentLastGood, the attempted bad source and observed failure, then final render and ordinary recovery. Correct wording/line of the separate diagnostic outcomes is not required as a sibling verdict.

matrix.description: S11.html_error_message: The console identifies undefinedFunctionCall from the complete HTML source.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actually run the exact complete HTML document and observe the corresponding diagnostic, not merely source containing undefinedFunctionCall.

matrix.description: S11.html_error_line: The error identifies line 6 of the exact complete HTML document, including its markup.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: The observed error must correspond to the exact nine-line document and its user line 6, with no added blank lines. No rollback sibling pass is required.

matrix.description: S11.html_error_rollback: The HTML failure restores recorded currentLastGood, not Failed HTML candidate; an ordinary recovery Run works.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actual successful baseline, attempted complete HTML and observed failure, retained/restored DOM and ordinary recovery. Static restoration is valid.

matrix.description: S12.timer_error_message: The timer callback's thrown async-error-marker is reported as a failure.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actually invoke the two-line source and observe the timer's async-error-marker failure after its 50 ms delay. A generic idle state is not an error result.

matrix.description: S12.timer_error_line: The timer error identifies entered user-source line 2.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: An actual callback error corresponding to the exact two-line source supplies the line-2 attribution target. No full diagnostic/rollback verdict is inherited.

matrix.description: S12.timer_error_rollback: The timer failure restores recorded currentLastGood, not async-failed-candidate; an ordinary recovery Run works.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actual successful baseline and actual callback failure precede final render comparison and working recovery; simply leaving the initial preview untouched cannot pass.

matrix.description: S13.promise_error_message: The unhandled promise-error-marker rejection is reported as a failure.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actually invoke the two-line Promise fixture and observe its unhandled-rejection failure. No inference from Promise.reject in the editor is allowed.

matrix.description: S13.promise_error_line: The unhandled rejection identifies entered user-source line 2.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: The actual unhandled-rejection event corresponds to entered line 2, not wrapper text or an unrelated prior error.

matrix.description: S13.promise_error_rollback: The rejection restores recorded currentLastGood, not promise-failed-candidate; an ordinary recovery Run works.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: An actual successful baseline and observed failing Promise attempt precede final render comparison and ordinary recovery. Source insertion without Run is not a failure trigger.

matrix.description: S14.console_level_stream: The four authored console levels have their exact values, order and unambiguous level indicators; console.error alone is a log.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: The authored Run actually produces all four new exact marker entries with order/levels. No distinct negative control is needed for this positive stream outcome.

matrix.description: S15.console_value_inspection: App controls expose object properties, nested deep value and array elements rather than opaque summaries.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actual logged object/array entries are inspected with app controls to reveal their nested values. Reading authored object literals is not execution/inspection evidence.

matrix.description: S16.console_history: Previously observed log entries remain while subsequent Runs actually append their distinct new markers, until Clear is used.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: Observe the initial rows and actual distinct appended markers from subsequent Runs; then verify the initial rows remain. A frozen console with no new entries cannot pass preservation.

matrix.description: S16.console_duration: The completed Run shows a measured duration, not a blank or placeholder.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: An actual completed authored Run supplies the duration being observed. A blank/static placeholder or a Run label without completed execution is insufficient.

matrix.description: S16.console_scroll_policy: New rows follow at the bottom; when deliberately scrolled up, incoming rows preserve the reading position.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Establish actual scroll position away from the bottom and actual new incoming rows, then actual bottom position and another new row. Nonoverflowing content or absent new rows does not prove a scroll policy.

matrix.description: S16.console_clear_control: Ordinary Clear removes prior rows; unrelated duration/status labels may remain.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: A confirmed nonempty console precedes ordinary Clear, and those actual rows disappear. Empty-before/empty-after is not clearing evidence.

matrix.description: S17.autorun_debounce: Enabled Auto-run waits for a typing pause, resets its wait on closer-spaced edits, then executes only the final version within about two seconds.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Real enabled automatic execution is observed, and timed closer-spaced edits demonstrate reset/final execution. An assumed debounce duration or automation-created idle gap is not evidence.

matrix.description: S17.autorun_off_stays_idle: First observe an authored edit execute automatically with Auto-run on and no manual Run. Then edits made with Auto-run already off remain unexecuted throughout the measured-delay-plus-margin window, and deliberate Run executes that exact pending source. A dead Auto-run feature cannot pass; correct debounce-reset behaviour is not a prerequisite.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: At least one genuine enabled automatic execution establishes capability and a measured delay; an off-state valid edit stays unrun for the window and then executes manually. Correct debounce-reset sibling scoring is not required.

matrix.description: S17.autorun_off_cancels_queue: After observing an authored edit execute automatically with Auto-run on, disable it before a further edit's measured debounce expires. That queued edit stays unexecuted for the full observation window and then executes through deliberate Run. A dead Auto-run feature cannot pass; correct debounce-reset behaviour is not a prerequisite.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: Real enabled automatic execution and measured timing establish that the later valid edit was eligible and pending when disabled; no execution follows through the window, and manual Run works. An inert Auto-run mode cannot pass.

matrix.description: S17.manual_run_independent_of_autorun: Ordinary Run executes authored code with Auto-run both on and off; the on-state proof has no pending edit debounce.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actual manual-triggered new executions in both offered states; the on-state source is unchanged after automatic work settles, avoiding debounce attribution. No queued-auto cancellation by manual Run is demanded.

matrix.description: S18.pane_dividers_work: Dividers change editor/preview and preview/console allocations while the panes remain usable.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Record initial allocations and actual user-caused changes while panes remain usable. Decorative drag handles without changed proportions cannot pass.

matrix.description: S18.pane_sizes_persist: The changed allocations survive reload; no exact pixels or layout are prescribed.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: An actually observed changed allocation precedes reload and survives it. Unchanged default sizes are not a persistence control.

matrix.description: S19.editor_monospace: The populated editor uses a monospaced face.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: A genuinely populated editor provides visible glyphs to inspect. An empty editor cannot establish the requested typography.

matrix.description: S19.editor_line_numbers: The editor displays actual line numbers for entered source.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Known actual entered lines are displayed with corresponding real line numbers. No separate editing-feature verdict is required.

matrix.description: S19.editor_syntax_colouring: JS, complete HTML and CSS each have visible syntax colouring under their corresponding filenames.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actual representative source is entered under each language filename and its different token classes are visibly coloured. No execution is required for editor syntax evidence.

matrix.description: S19.editor_matching_brackets: A cursor beside either brace visibly identifies the matching pair.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: A complete matching pair exists and the cursor is actually placed beside either brace before inspecting the indicator. An unmatched brace is invalid setup.

matrix.description: S20.editor_multiline_indent: Tab consistently indents all three selected lines without changing source. Retaining selection is not required.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Three actual selected source lines have a recorded initial form and visibly gain one consistent indent without code loss. Selection retention is not a prerequisite.

matrix.description: S20.editor_multiline_unindent: Shift+Tab removes a consistent indent from all three selected lines. Reselect/manual-indent if needed to isolate this action.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Three actually indented selected lines precede Shift+Tab and lose one matching level. Reselection or manually establishing indentation isolates a failed Tab action.

matrix.description: S21.saved_record_fidelity: New drafts save as distinct exact records; loading restores each one's fields. S23's current Save updates its existing identity rather than adding another.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actual distinct New/Save identities and exact loaded fields; S23's actual current Save updates the loaded identity. The stale-refusal verdict is not borrowed.

matrix.description: S21.saved_records_browser_reload: Both saved identities and exact fields remain retrievable after browser reload.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: The two records actually exist before reload and are freshly retrieved afterward with exact fields/identities. An empty library staying empty cannot pass.

matrix.description: S22.process_restart_durability: The one process restart preserves recorded identities/fields/revisions exactly once; a current post-restart Save changes only its target and persists.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Own New/Save controls and a successful pre-restart update establish exact identities/revisions; the actual restart completes; reads and a valid post-restart update follow. No Duplicate/Delete/execution control is required.

matrix.description: S23.stale_save_server_refusal: An otherwise-valid stale Save is refused with newer fields/revision unchanged. The successful newer Save is its control; S21 owns update fidelity.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: A real newer Save advances the same identity/revision; an otherwise-valid captured old-revision write is actually sent/refused and newer data is freshly read unchanged. A guessed route or unrelated invalid field cannot pass.

matrix.description: S23.stale_save_draft_recovery: The actual dirty editor gets useful conflict feedback, retains all unsaved fields and supports deliberate latest-revision recovery; proactive prevention is valid.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actual two-editor shared-old-revision state, B's captured real dirty fields, A's newer successful Save, B's UI conflict path, preserved fields and deliberate latest-revision recovery. Proactive prevention is valid without forcing a disabled Save.

matrix.description: S24.title_trimming: Padded unused titles are stored/displayed trimmed after both creation and rename.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Successful create and rename using padded unused titles, followed by exact fresh stored/displayed reads. Rejected writes or labels alone cannot prove normalization.

matrix.description: S24.rename_title_only: Current rename changes only the selected title, preserving its filename/source and the complete sibling record.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: An actual successful selected-title change with recorded before/after fields and sibling snapshot. A no-op rename cannot establish preservation-under-rename.

matrix.description: S24.title_collision_refusal: With an observed successful valid current title write and unused-title recovery, UI and current-revision server writes refuse exact/padded collisions with useful feedback and both complete records/revisions unchanged.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: A known working valid current title write and successful unused-title recovery, existing target title, actual current-revision collisions and fresh complete unchanged state. Unrelated invalidity or all-write refusal is insufficient.

matrix.description: S24.title_empty_rejected: With an observed successful valid current title write and unused-title recovery, otherwise-valid empty and whitespace-only titles are refused without saved-state mutation.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: A working valid current title write and successful unused-title recovery establish the operation; each empty/whitespace attempt uses otherwise-valid current data and leaves fresh state unchanged.

matrix.description: S24.title_case_sensitive: A case-distinct title coexists under its own identity and exact fields.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Both case-distinct titles actually save/coexist with different identities and their own exact fields. A case label in an unsaved draft is insufficient.

matrix.description: S25.stale_rename_refusal: A valid stale rename is usefully refused without newer-record mutation; current renames before/after work.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Current rename works before and after; the old revision of the same identity is actually used for a different unused valid name; newer fields/revision remain unchanged.

matrix.description: S26.duplicate_initial_fidelity: Duplicate creates a distinct stable identity with its chosen title and the original exact filename/source.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: The original exists with captured source/filename, and a real duplicate creates a distinct identity with the chosen title and exact initial fields. A renamed original is not a copy.

matrix.description: S26.duplicate_edit_independence: Each own edit actually saves and reloads: changing Original preserves Copy's previous source, and then changing Copy preserves Original's independently saved source.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: Each own update actually persists and reloads in its target before checking the other record is unchanged, in both directions. Ignoring both saves cannot earn noninterference credit.

matrix.description: S26.duplicate_collision_refusal: Duplicate/create refuses the existing copy title without overwrite or extra same-title record; a new unused title succeeds.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: The copy title already exists, the observed duplicate/create operation is real, collision is attempted with valid fields, and an unused-title duplicate succeeds. No blanket create refusal can pass.

matrix.description: S27.delete_confirmation_cancel: Delete asks first, and cancellation leaves the complete library and exact records unchanged after reload.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: An existing target and actual offered confirmation precede Cancel; complete records remain. The same protocol's confirmed removal establishes that the target operation is real, without inheriting its full selected-only verdict.

matrix.description: S27.delete_confirmed_selected_only: The actual confirmed removal deletes only the selected identity durably, preserving sibling/unrelated records. Confirmation availability is separately owned.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: An existing selected identity and full library snapshot precede an actual removal; fresh lookup/reload show only that identity gone. Missing confirmation UI is separately scored.

matrix.description: S28.stale_delete_refusal: A valid stale delete is usefully refused without newer-record mutation; current deletes before/after work. Confirmation is not scored here.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: An actual current delete control works; the target then receives a real newer revision; a valid old-revision delete is refused; a deliberate current delete afterward succeeds.

matrix.description: S29.deleted_identity_update_refusal: Updating the removed identity is usefully refused without resurrection, replacement or unrelated mutation; an existing-record update works.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: An observed valid update and confirmed actual removal establish the identity's history; the replay is otherwise valid; no identity/replacement appears; an existing sibling update still works.

matrix.description: S30.dirty_workspace_identity: The edited record is identifiable and source-only, title-only and filename-only changes each show unsaved state.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: A known clean loaded record is actually changed in each single field, then its identity/dirty indication is observed. A permanently dirty label cannot substitute for the controlled clean-to-dirty changes.

matrix.description: S30.dirty_transition_protection: Each of four replacement routes warns, and cancellation preserves all dirty fields. Re-establish each fixture independently.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Exact dirty fields and real destinations exist for each route; warning/Cancel preserves them, and the protocol's accepted route establishes that replacement is an actual operation. Rebuild each fixture; do not inherit a whole accepted-transition sibling verdict.

matrix.description: S30.dirty_transition_acceptance: Accepting each replacement reaches its actual destination, while discarded edits never change saved Base. No new-draft template is prescribed.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: An actual dirty draft and chosen destination precede an accepted route; destination fields/identity are freshly observed and saved Base remains unchanged. No warning-presence sibling verdict is required.

matrix.description: S31.native_dirty_leave_protection: Dirty work gets native leave protection: dismiss retains the draft, accept permits reload, saved data stays intact; clean reload does not warn.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: A clean actual reload, real keyboard-made dirty work, native warning/dismissal with retained draft, then accepted actual reload and saved-state read. A custom app dialog or automation timeout alone is not the native control.

matrix.description: S32.export_exact_source_file: An actual unsaved-draft export downloads the exact filename and unchanged source, not merely a toast.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: The actual current draft has known filename/text, then a real browser download is observed and compared. Saved library state and import success are not prerequisites.

matrix.description: S33.supported_file_import: Lowercase supported import supplies exact filename/source in an editable draft; its subsequent edit can be saved/reloaded.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: An actual supported upload produces known filename/source; a real edit is saved and freshly retrieved. Lowercase setup isolates uppercase policy failure.

matrix.description: S33.import_off_no_execution: After the supported file actually appears in the draft, its authored markers remain unexecuted and the recorded successful preview remains for the off-state window; deliberate Run then produces that same imported source's DOM/log markers.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: Actual successful preview plus actual supported import; the source remains unrun through the off-state window, then that same imported source really executes on deliberate Run. Neither an ignored upload nor disabled execution can pass.

matrix.description: S33.import_unsupported_extension: After the same importer has actually accepted a supported control file, an unsupported import gets useful refusal while the current title, filename and source remain unchanged.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: The same importer actually accepts a supported file before its unsupported-file refusal and exact current-draft preservation are observed. Full edit/save fidelity of the sibling import result is not a control requirement.

matrix.description: S33.saved_filename_extension_rejection: With an observed valid supported-filename write and successful valid recovery, an otherwise-valid current server write refuses unsupported.txt without field/revision mutation. A lowercase control is valid.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: An actual valid supported-filename write and valid recovery establish the observed operation; current otherwise-valid unsupported.txt write is refused without fresh-state mutation. Use the independent saved fallback if import fails.

matrix.description: S33.saved_filename_path_rejection: With an observed valid supported-filename write and successful valid recovery, an otherwise-valid current server write refuses nested/demo.js without field/revision mutation. A lowercase control is valid.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: An actual valid supported-filename write and valid recovery establish the observed operation; current otherwise-valid nested/demo.js write is refused without fresh-state mutation. Refresh state after any prior accepted invalid write.

matrix.description: S33.source_file_extension_case: Uppercase .JS is accepted by import and saved unchanged. Test saving from a lowercase-imported draft if importer case handling fails.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Uppercase import and uppercase saved readback are both actual positive observations. A lowercase-imported draft can establish the server leg independently if uppercase import fails.

matrix.description: S34.theme_actual_switch: The control switches chrome, editor and console into both actual appearances; either may be the starting theme.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: The starting appearance is recorded and actual workspace/editor/console changes are observed in both directions. A changing toggle label is not sufficient.

matrix.description: S34.theme_work_preserved: During two actually observed theme changes, the recorded exact draft fields and existing successful preview/console output remain intact. Preview recolouring is not required.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: The exact draft plus successful preview and nonempty console exist before actual visible theme changes; their preserved state is compared afterward. The full appearance-coverage sibling verdict is not inherited.

matrix.description: S35.shortcut_run: The discoverable documented Run binding alone produces keyboard-marker and keyboard-log without clicking Run.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: The documented binding is actually invoked on known entered source and produces its DOM/log without the button. No assumed conventional binding or delayed automatic run is accepted.

matrix.description: S35.shortcut_save: The discoverable documented Save binding alone saves the exact draft fields without clicking Save.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Known fresh draft fields are actually saved by the documented binding and freshly read. No Run-shortcut pass or preceding execution of this source is required.

matrix.description: S35.shortcut_clear: The discoverable documented Clear binding alone removes prior rows without clicking Clear.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Known nonempty rows precede the actual documented Clear binding. Ordinary manual Run may seed the control if the Run shortcut failed, without earning that shortcut credit.

matrix.description: S36.callback_shared_run_deadline: After the four-second callback actually emits late-callback-entered, it shares the original Run budget: timely termination/reason, no resumption and successful recovery; no fresh callback clock.
matrix.disposition: Explicit descriptor repair plus mandatory protocol controls
matrix.required_actual_controls: The actual delayed callback emits late-callback-entered after its four-second wait; the measured original-Run clock, timeout reason, no resumption and ordinary recovery follow. A generic timeout with no dispatched callback is insufficient.

matrix.description: S36.callback_timeout_rollback: The timed-out callback retains/restores recorded currentLastGood rather than failed-loop-candidate; provisional display is optional.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: An actual successful baseline and actual entered callback/failure precede the resulting render comparison. The full shared-deadline timing verdict is not required as control; the callback must actually occur.

matrix.description: S37.interaction_latest_rollback: After a successful interaction commits interaction-committed, the later failure retains/restores that state, not initial or provisional/late DOM.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: Initial successful Run and a real successful Commit change establish interaction-committed; the later actual Start work interaction fails and the result is compared with that latest commit. Initial state alone cannot pass.

matrix.description: S37.interaction_budget_no_extension: Later accepted, ignored or blocked input cannot extend the pending interaction's budget; timeout/reason, no late resumption and ordinary recovery are observed.
matrix.disposition: Existing outcome retained; its relevant protocol controls are mandatory
matrix.required_actual_controls: An actual successful interaction context and Start work marker/pending state precede the second input attempt or observed prevention; measure its unchanged original clock, timeout, absence of late work and recovery. Blocking second input is valid only after actual work has started.
